page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.2xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on the ARM64 architecture using the AWS Neoverse-N1 model, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 3750 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the im4gn.2xlarge demonstrates average multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth is robust, delivering 472.87 GB/sec for cached read-only operations and 121.23 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and compression tasks show lower efficiency, as evidenced by weak gzip compression and poor single-threaded bzip3 decompression speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high local storage density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for storage-heavy workloads without paying for excess CPU capacity. It is well-suited for database operations, as reflected in its average Passmark database and Redis SET performance of 9.97 million operations per second. The instance is also optimized for static web serving and medium-scale transactional databases, though it is less suitable for compute-intensive tasks, heavy single-threaded processing, or large language model inference.
